name: The Saffron Undertow
image_style: A mixed-media desktop illustration combining drypoint engraving, translucent casein paint, and thin layers of iridescent mica powder on rough blue-grey paper. Fine scratched linework describes masonry, rigging, wool, and weathered wood; matte painted passages build broad atmospheric shapes, while mica catches only select wet surfaces and metal edges. The mood is maritime, antiquarian, quietly uncanny, and deadpan, with a serious historical world interrupted by an unmistakably misplaced visitor. Use a rare palette of drowned blue-black, storm-slate, sour saffron, chalked rose, oxidized mint, and tiny vermilion signals. Keep the upper edge broad, quiet, and low-detail for a desktop panel, with a calm dark region on the left for widgets. No lettering, logos, watermarks, frames, sacred parody, or interface elements.
scene: Exactly one striking 16:10 landscape wallpaper, preferably 2560x1600, set inside a late-medieval tidal engineering house on a storm-battered estuary. A long timber-and-stone sluice hall contains enormous wooden tide gates, counterweights, hand-cut gearing, drainage channels, wet flagstones, brass gauges, coiled hemp rope, and carefully rendered workers in historically grounded coastal clothing. Through open arches, a broad grey-green estuary and distant fishing boats disappear into rain. In the lower-right, Space Ghost is unmistakable in his muscular white costume, black hood and mask, yellow cape, and red power bands, solemnly operating a gigantic wooden hand pump with both hands while a small soaked engineer points toward the correct lever. His cape is pinned under a practical iron weight, and the workers continue their dignified emergency repairs with restrained bewilderment. The humor comes only from his absolute seriousness and misplaced hydraulic expertise. Christian and historical subjects remain reverent and secular; no holy figures, devotional attributes, worship, lettering, logos, UI, watermark, or frame. Keep the upper third spacious and nearly empty, with the strongest detail along the lower two-thirds.
